newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans, meal climb further on exports, cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans, meal climb further on exports, cash.

text.p: CBOT soybean and soymeal futures climbed further in fast dealings on talk China bought U.S. soybeans and on firm cash basis levels, traders said.
"Those three cargoes of beans sold to China are doing it," a floor trader said.

U.S. exporters could not confirm the sale. Some sources said it was unlikely China purchased U.S. supplies as Brazilian soybeans are cheaper, but floor sources cited "reliability of supply", saying China needed prompt shipment and could not wait for Brazilian soybeans.
Both pits were also supported by technical indicators. Pit sources said soybeans broke through resistance at $8.54 per bushel in the July and the next upside objective was $8.80.
"We're going back up to test those highs," a trader said, referring to 8-1/2 year highs notched in recent weeks. "We shattered resistance and there's not much in the way now."
In soymeal, chartists put resistance at $277.00 per ton in the July.
At 1031 CDT, soybeans were up 17-3/4 to 1-1/4 cents per bushel with May up 17-3/4 at $8.64-3/4. Soymeal was up $6.30 to $1.10 per ton with May up $6.30 at $279.30.
